title: Huang Apologizes to Nvidia Staff After Returning as CEO (Video)
Asian Stocks Resume Slide as AI Concerns Hit Chipmakers
text: Stocks sold off as doubts over the durability of the artificial intelligence boom drove investors out of technology shares. MSCI’s gauge of Asia Pacific equities fell 2.1%, led by a 6.3% slide in South Korea and a 4.8% drop in Taiwan, the region’s two key barometers of the AI trade. Bloomberg's Winnie Hsu reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Houthis Hit Saudi Finance Center, Extending Tit-for-Tat Attacks
text: The Houthis struck Saudi Arabia’s main finance district for the second time in a week on Tuesday, extending a cycle of tit-for-tat attacks and complicating the kingdom’s push to establish its capital as a global business center.

title: Dangote Refinery Said to List in Lagos on December 1
text: Bloomberg understands billionaire Aliko Dangote’s oil refinery will start trading in Lagos as soon as next week. Dangote Petroleum Refinery & Petrochemicals debut is being set for December 1, in what will be Africa’s biggest IPO. Chief Africa correspondent, Jennifer Zabasajja reports from Johannesburg. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: GPIF Agenda May Signal Portfolio Review Progress, JPMorgan Says
text: Japan’s largest pension fund may be moving closer to deciding whether to revise its asset allocation, according to JPMorgan Chase & Co., potentially reviving speculation that it could steer more of its ¥314 trillion ($2 trillion) portfolio toward domestic bonds.
